title: Climate Resilience Act 2018 (No. 16 of 2018)
citation: Climate Resilience Act 2018 (Act No. 16 of 2018), assented 19 December 2018; commenced 1 January 2019 by the Climate Resilience (Commencement) Order 2019 (SRO 3 of 2019)
evidence: SRO 3 of 2019 (gazetted 10 January 2019, https://dominica.gov.dm/laws/2019/Climate%20Resilience%20(Commencement)%20Order,%202019%20S.R.O.%203%20of%202019.pdf), section 2: "The Climate Resilience Act 2018 is deemed to have come into operation on the 1st day of January, 2019." Act section 24: "This Act shall come into force on such date as the Prime Minister may, by Order published in the Gazette, appoint."
notes: Language: English, the only official language of Dominican legislation; no second official language and no government translation exists, so there is no other-language or translation record. One record, the Act as published (Part I to VI, sections 1 to 25), fetched from the Laws of Dominica portal. The Act sets up the Dominica Climate Resilience Policy Board and the Climate Resilience Execution Agency for Dominica (CREAD) and binds the State (section 23); it has no duty on companies. Section 25: "This Act shall continue in force for a period of four years from the date of its commencement, unless the Prime Minister extends it for one further year by Order subject to negative resolution of the House." Four years from 2019-01-01 ends 2022-12-31; SRO 44 of 2021 (dm-climate-resilience-extension-order-2021) extends it one year to 2023-12-31, which is the one extension section 25 allows. No later extension order, no amending Act and no repeal was found: the portal title search for 'climate' lists only the Act and these two orders, and the Printery SRO previews for 2023 hold no climate text (six scanned previews unread). The Act is therefore recorded as lapsed after 2023-12-31. Whether CREAD was wound down or continues under another instrument was not found on any official page.
status_note: Lapsed: the Act ceased to have effect after 2023-12-31 under section 25 once the one permitted extension (SRO 44 of 2021) ran out; no later extension found on 2026-11-03. No repeal record is stored because the lapse comes from the Act's own duration clause.

title: Climate Resilience (Extension of duration) Order, 2021 (SRO 44 of 2021)
citation: SRO 44 of 2021, made 22 November 2021 under section 25 of the Climate Resilience Act 2018; gazetted 1 December 2021
evidence: SRO 44 of 2021 states "(Gazetted 1st December, 2021.)" and section 3: "The Act is hereby extended for one further year until the 31st day of December, 2023." The Order has no commencement clause, so the Gazette date is taken as the date it took effect.
notes: Language: English, the only official language of Dominican legislation; no second official language and no government translation exists, so there is no other-language or translation record. One record, the whole Order (three sections). It extends the Climate Resilience Act 2018 to 2023-12-31; section 25 of the Act allows one extension only, so no further extension order can be valid without an amending Act.

title: Physical Planning Act 2002 (No. 5 of 2002)
citation: Physical Planning Act 2002 (Act No. 5 of 2002), assented 9 May 2002, gazetted 16 May 2002
evidence: The Act prints "I assent ... 9th May, 2002" and "(Gazetted 16th May, 2002)". It has no commencement clause and no commencement order was found on the portal, so the Gazette date is taken as the first in-force date.
notes: Language: English, the only official language of Dominican legislation; no second official language and no government translation exists, so there is no other-language or translation record. One record, the whole Act as published. Dominica has no single environment act. This Act carries the environmental protection duties on developers: section 23 requires an environmental impact assessment for developments in the Second Schedule and where the Authority expects significant environmental harm, and Part VI (sections 46 to 61, headed Environmental Protection) covers environmental protection areas and ministerial orders to protect the environment. The portal lists no amending Act, so the as-published text is the only version stored; an amendment passed after the portal list was not excluded. The Environmental Health Services Act 1997 (dm-environmental-health-services-act-1997) carries the pollution and discharge duties.

title: Environmental Health Services Act 1997 (No. 8 of 1997)
citation: Environmental Health Services Act 1997 (Act No. 8 of 1997), assented 15 October 1997, gazetted 16 October 1997
evidence: The Act prints "15th October, 1997" under the President's assent and "(Gazetted 16th October, 1997)" (read from the OCR text of the scanned PDF). No commencement clause appears in the arrangement of sections or the OCR text, so the Gazette date is taken as the first in-force date.
notes: Language: English, the only official language of Dominican legislation; no second official language and no government translation exists, so there is no other-language or translation record. One record, the whole Act as published. The text is uncorrected OCR output of a scanned official PDF (38 image pages, no text layer; ocrmypdf --force-ocr -l eng, tesseract 5.3.4): the OCR has errors such as stray marks in the arrangement of sections and was not corrected or reflowed by hand. Part II (Environmental Health Matters) holds the section headed 'Prohibitions and obligations in the interest of the environment' and the section on notification of an emission or discharge of a contaminant or pollutant; the Environmental Health Services regulations of 2003 to 2022 are separate instruments and were not added.

title: ECCB Prudential Standard on Climate-Related and Environmental Risks for Institutions Licensed under the Banking Act, 2015
citation: Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, Prudential Standard on Climate-Related and Environmental Risks (August 2023), for institutions licensed under the Banking Act, 2015 (Dominica: Banking Act 2015, Act 4 of 2015)
evidence: Section 1.0 Commencement: "This Prudential Standard shall come into effect on the 1st day of March, 2024." Read in a PDF copy at https://data.sbfnetwork.org/sites/default/files/survey-attachments/2025-05/2024-07-30-11-23-57-Prudential-Standard-on-Climate-related-and-Environmental-Risks.pdf on 2026-11-03, because https://www.eccb-centralbank.org answers HTTP 403 from the cloud address; no official ECCB page could be opened to confirm the date.
notes: Regional instrument of the eight ECCU members (AG DM GD KN LC VC and the territories AI MS): the same standard sits in the scope of each of those places that has one. The copy lists the Dominica Banking Act as "Banking (Amendment) Act, 2015 of the Commonwealth of Dominica (No 4 of 2015)". Sections 5.1 to 5.6 set duties on licensed financial institutions for board oversight, risk management, stress testing, disclosure (5.5) and reporting (5.6). The official_url is the ECCB Enforced page used for Grenada; it also returned 403, so the page was not opened. Row DM-ECCB-ADOPTED is permission requested; no text stored. The Eastern Caribbean Securities Regulatory Commission (https://www.ecsrc.com) and the Eastern Caribbean Securities Exchange (https://www.ecseonline.com) opened; their home pages and rule lists show no ESG or climate rule, which is a title check only.
